reason: The support cells and connective fibers appear to be complementary parts of the skin's supporting tissue.
expectation: They will form a supportive layer for the skin.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed the skin's supporting layer, so I can now work on its surface.
reaction: The tug panels make the support layer's role clearer.
reason: Cell junctions appear suited to connecting the neighboring surface cells.
expectation: The junctions will join the surface cells into a sheet.

effect: The junctions connected the surface cells into a sheet, giving me a layer to combine with the supporting skin layer.
reaction: The tug and magnified seam make the junctions' role clear.
reason: The connected surface and supporting layers appear to be complementary parts of the skin.
expectation: The two layers will form a skin structure.

effect: The surface layer needed the tough outer layer first, producing a surface barrier; I can now try attaching it to the supporting layer.
reaction: I was surprised the outer layer had to be added before the support layer.
reason: The surface barrier and supporting skin layer appear to be complementary parts of the skin.
expectation: They will form a layered skin structure.

effect: The barrier and supporting layer formed layered skin, with vessels supplying the living surface cells from below.
reaction: The cross-section makes the connection between the layers clear.
reason: The skin needs sensory endings to detect contact.
expectation: The endings will give the layered skin a way to sense touch.

effect: The sensory endings made sensitive skin, completing the first goal; the arm now needs protection and supplies.
reaction: The fingertip picture connects the protective skin to its sensing role.
reason: The sensitive skin should provide the working arm with its protective covering.
expectation: The skin will cover the arm and connect touch sensing to it.

effect: The sensitive skin currently has no available operation as the first item, so I need to check how the arm can receive protection and supplies.
reaction: The lack of a compatibility hint is a little confusing.
reason: The arm may need its supply network before the skin can be added; inspecting it will reveal its available partners.
expectation: The inspection will show what can currently be combined with the arm.

alternatives.reason: The supply network appears relevant to the goal, but I am unsure of the required order.

effect: The arm needed the body supply network first, and inspection automatically combined them into a supplied arm.
reaction: The required order is clearer now.
reason: The supplied arm still needs the protective and touch-sensitive skin.
expectation: The skin will cover the supplied arm and add touch sensing.

effect: The supplied arm and sensitive skin formed a living body model, completing the protection and supplies goal. The remaining goal is to hold the glass steady.
reaction: The cutaway brings the previously built systems together clearly.
reason: The glass is the object the living body model needs to hold.
expectation: The model will use contact feedback to hold the glass steady.

effect: The final combination completed the goal and showed how touch feedback and muscle tension help keep a slipping glass steady.
reaction: The slipping-glass sequence made the purpose of contact feedback concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was most worthwhile because it brought touch signals and muscle action together in a familiar task.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to add skin was the most confusing passage: it gave no compatibility hint, leaving the required order unclear until I inspected the arm.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the surface layer needed the tough outer layer before it could join the supporting layer.

arbitrary.text: Adding the supply network before the skin felt like a required ordering without a clear explanation for why the skin could not be added first.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it continued to connect familiar actions to the body systems involved; the glass example made those connections meaningful.
